original_question: Let p be a prime, let P_* be the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra with P_* congruent to F_p[xi_1, xi_2, xi_3, ...], let P be its dual Hopf algebra, and consider Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p). The p-th power map on P_* induces an endomorphism P^0: Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) -> Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p, F_p). For fixed s > 0, is every element z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) eventually sent to a nilpotent element by some iterate of P^0; equivalently, whenever z lies in the preimage (P^0)^-1 Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), must z be nilpotent?
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("The problems presented by John H Palmieri"), specifically Conjecture 4.1, with the notation fixed in the introductory paragraph of Section 4; Theorem 4.2 gives the p = 2 case, and Conjecture 4.3 is the stronger neighboring variant with n = 1.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the main target very closely: it uses the same Hopf algebra P dual to the polynomial part P_* of the dual Steenrod algebra, the same endomorphism P^0 induced by the pth-power map on P_*, the same bigraded Ext group Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), the same restriction s > 0, and the same two equivalent formulations that appear in the paper: eventual nilpotence under iterates of P^0, and nilpotence of elements in the P^0-preimage.
missing_details: The paper quantifies over all internal degrees t; this should be stated explicitly rather than left implicit.
The class z should be understood as a homogeneous (bigraded) element of Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p).
Nilpotent means nilpotent in the graded algebra Ext_P^{*,*}(F_p, F_p), not merely in a fixed bidegree.
The phrase "some iterate" should be made precise as: there exists an integer n >= 0, depending on z, such that (P^0)^n(z) is nilpotent.
The preimage formulation needs clarification because P^0 changes internal degree: saying z lies in (P^0)^-1(Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p)) means precisely that P^0(z) has bidegree (s,t).
To be fully paper-faithful as a research problem, it helps to note that Theorem 4.2 already proves Conjecture 4.1 when p = 2, so the genuinely open content is the odd-prime case.
The draft does not distinguish Conjecture 4.1 from the stronger neighboring Conjecture 4.3, which asks whether one can always take n = 1.
refined_question: Let p be a prime, let P_* be the polynomial part of the dual Steenrod algebra, so that P_* is isomorphic to F_p[xi_1, xi_2, xi_3, ...], and let P denote its graded dual Hopf algebra. The Frobenius pth-power map on P_* induces an algebra endomorphism P^0: Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p) -> Ext_P^{s,pt}(F_p, F_p). Fix a homological degree s > 0. Is it true that for every internal degree t and every homogeneous class z in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), there exists an integer n >= 0 such that (P^0)^n(z) is nilpotent in the bigraded algebra Ext_P^{*,*}(F_p, F_p)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for fixed s > 0 and every t, if a homogeneous class z satisfies P^0(z) in Ext_P^{s,t}(F_p, F_p), then z is nilpotent.
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Palmieri's Conjecture 4.1 in Section 4: the paper introduces exactly the same notation P_*, P, and P^0, and Conjecture 4.1 is stated in exactly the same eventual-nilpotence / preimage-nilpotence form. Theorem 4.2 then records that this conjecture is true for p = 2, while Conjecture 4.3 is a strictly stronger version asserting that one may always take n = 1. Because your draft asks only for eventual nilpotence under some iterate, it targets Conjecture 4.1 rather than the stronger Conjecture 4.3.
